## PUNIU HiFi-DAS

The PUNIU reader supports differential HDF5 version 1 files with a two-dimensional `/default` dataset. [HiFi-DAS](https://puniutech.com/en/products/hifi-das-v2-0/) is PUNIU's TGD-OFDR distributed acoustic sensing system.

The output dimensions are `time` and `distance`. Distance is in metres relative to the first recorded channel of each file, with spacing `round(spatial_sampling_rate, 1) * step` (halfway values round away from zero). Original channel numbers are preserved in the auxiliary `channel` coordinate. Selecting a window preserves the file-relative distance origin. Files with different starting channels require spatial alignment before merging.

Time is constructed from integer `epoch` seconds and `ns` nanoseconds without a timezone adjustment. The file does not establish a timezone or signal unit; amplitudes are preserved without calibration. The reader requires explicit axis-order attributes and a sampling interval representable as integer nanoseconds. `spatial_resolution` maps to gauge length, following the acquisition reader's convention.

```python
import dascore as dc

spool = dc.read("recording.h5", file_format="PUNIU", distance=(100, 200))
```

`dc.scan` reads metadata without loading the signal. Time, distance, and channel intervals are applied before reading the HDF5 data; an interval outside the recording returns an empty spool.
